haiku-low.q1: Pages of up to 500 products, ordered by id via keyset pagination. One request at a time, never two in parallel.
haiku-low.q2: In sync_state as cursor, the id of the last product saved in staging. Each page and its cursor are written in one transaction.
haiku-low.q3: The change feed starts at start_seq, taken when the download began, and catch-up applies changes in change_seq order. Only visible changes are returned, so late-saved changes are not skipped.
haiku-low.q4: The server replies 410 resync_required. The client empties staging, clears cursor and catchup_seq, gets a new start_seq, and restarts the full download. products is unchanged.
haiku-low.q5: Built in products_staging: emptied, then re-downloaded from the start. It becomes live when the swap transaction copies staging into products after catch-up.
haiku-low.q6: App launch or return to foreground, when mode is incremental. At most one run every 15 minutes, counted from run start, including failed runs.
haiku-low.q7: It resends the same request unchanged, waiting 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds: 5 attempts total. Then it stops, keeps saved data, and waits for the next trigger.
haiku-low.q8: It pauses. An in-flight request may finish and be saved. It resumes when Wi-Fi returns, even if the app is not open.
haiku-low.q9: By change_seq. If the stored row's change_seq is equal or higher, it skips the change. Otherwise it applies it, deleting on tombstones.
haiku-low.q10: It starts from last_seq. last_seq is saved in the same transaction as each page of applied changes, so it moves forward after each page.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED for what the server reads. The feed returns visible changes in change_seq order. Deletes come back as tombstones with deleted = true, kept 7 days.

sonnet.q1: Keyset pagination: pages of up to 500 live products in id order (after_id=X&limit=500). One page at a time, never two at once, so no parallel fetching.
sonnet.q2: In the sync_state row as `cursor` (id of last product saved in staging). Each page's products are written to products_staging and cursor is set in the same transaction, so both happen or neither.
sonnet.q3: POST /catalogue/full/start records start_seq (highest visible change_seq) when the download begins. After the last page, catch-up applies changes since start_seq (via catchup_seq) to staging, using the higher-change_seq-wins apply rule, before the swap. Changes are served only in visible change_seq order, so late-saved changes are not skipped.
sonnet.q4: Server replies 410 with body resync_required. The client goes to step 6: mode=full, phase=downloading, empty staging, clear cursor and catchup_seq, call full/start for a new start_seq, and rerun the full download. products stays unchanged meanwhile.
sonnet.q5: It is built in the products_staging table (reps never see it), with catch-up changes applied. It becomes the live catalogue at the swap: one transaction that deletes old products rows, copies all staging rows into products, sets last_seq=catchup_seq, mode=incremental, and empties staging.
sonnet.q6: Triggered by app launch or return to foreground when mode is incremental. At most one run every 15 minutes (skipped if last_incremental_at is under 15 minutes ago; the time is saved when a run starts, even if it later fails). Any network may be used.
sonnet.q7: Retry the same request unchanged with waits of 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s: 5 attempts total (first try plus 4 retries), counted per request. After 5 failures it stops, keeps everything already saved, and waits for the next launch/foreground trigger.
sonnet.q8: The request already in flight may finish and be saved, then the download pauses. When Wi-Fi returns it resumes from the saved cursor, whether or not the app is open. Nothing is deleted.
sonnet.q9: Compare change_seq. If a row exists and the incoming change_seq is not greater than the stored one, skip it. Otherwise a tombstone deletes the row (no-op if none), and anything else is inserted or replaces the row.
sonnet.q10: It starts from last_seq (GET /catalogue/changes?since=last_seq). last_seq advances with each page, saved in the same transaction as that page's changes, so the next run continues from the last change applied.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED what the server reads internally to build the feed. What is stated: it returns only visible (saved) changes with change_seq greater than since, in change_seq order, up to 1,000 per call with has_more. Deletes are represented as tombstones (deleted = true rows), kept for 7 days.
